blocks.text: Introduction

Assalam o alaikum bachon! Aaj se hum ek naya unit shuru kar rahe hain: Conics. Is unit mein hum chaar mashhoor curves padhenge: circle, parabola, ellipse aur hyperbola. Yeh curves sirf kitabi cheezein nahin hain. Satellite ka orbit, torch ke andar ka reflector, pul (bridge) ke cable ki shakal, sab inhi curves se bante hain. Pehle dekhte hain ke yeh sab curves aate kahan se hain, phir circle se shuru karenge.

Kitab batati hai ke Greek mathematicians Apollonius (260-200 B.C.) aur Pappus (chauthi sadi A.D. ke shuru mein) ne conic sections par bohat kaam kiya, magar unhon ne Euclidean geometry (yani sirf shaklon aur compass-ruler wali geometry) istemal ki. Hum yahan analytic geometry istemal karenge, yani har curve ko coordinates aur equation ki shakal mein likh kar us ki properties nikalenge.

Conics ki theory ke bohat se applications hain, jaise space mechanics (khala mein cheezon ki harkat, satellites aur planets ke raaste), oceanography (samandar ka ilm) aur science aur technology ki bohat si doosri shaakhein.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Roz marra ki zindagi mein yeh curves kahan nazar aate hain? Chand dekhiye:
1. Circle: cycle ka pahiya, ghari ka dial, pani mein pathar phenkne se banne wali lehrein.
2. Parabola: hawa mein phenki gayi gend ka raasta, dish antenna aur torch ke reflector ki shakal.
3. Ellipse: zameen aur doosre planets ka suraj ke gird raasta; tirchha rakha hua gilaas jis mein pani ho, us ke pani ki satah.
4. Hyperbola: kuch cooling towers ki deewar ki shakal, aur kuch navigation systems.
Yaad rakhiye ke Apollonius ne yeh sab shaklon ki madad se padha tha; hum inhein equations se padhenge, jo hisaab lagane ke liye kahin zyada taaqatwar tareeqa hai: faasle, points aur angles seedhe calculate ho jate hain.

Ab kitab cone banane ka tareeqa batati hai. Ek circle lijiye jis ka centre C hai. C se ek line RS khenchiye jo circle ki plane par perpendicular (bilkul seedhi khari, 90 degree par) ho. Is line par ek fixed point A chun lijiye. Ab A se har mumkin seedhi line khenchiye jo circle ke kisi na kisi point ko chhooti ho. Yeh sab lines mil kar ek surface banati hain jise right circular cone kehte hain. Har aisi seedhi line cone ka generator (ya ruling) kehlati hai. Poori surface ke do alag hisse hote hain jinhein nappes kehte hain; yeh sirf point A par milte hain. Yeh milne wala point cone ka vertex hai aur asal line RS cone ka axis hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Kitab mein chhapa hai "draw a line RS passes through c"; sahi yeh hai: "line RS jo C (centre, capital C) se guzarti hai aur circle ki plane par perpendicular hai".
Kitab mein "the axis of come" chhapa hai; sahi lafz "cone" hai: "the axis of the cone".
Jab is cone ko kisi plane (seedhi chapti satah, jaise kaghaz ki sheet) se kaata jaye to kaat ki jagah jo curve banta hai use conic section (ya sirf conics) kehte hain.

Kuch khaas cases bhi hain jinhein degenerate conics kehte hain (degenerate yani "bigri hui" ya adhoori shakal). Yeh tab bante hain jab kaatne wali plane vertex A se guzarti hai. Tab khoobsurat curve ke bajaye sirf ek point, ek seedhi line, ya do aapas mein katti hui lines milti hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Is ko aise sochiye: do ice-cream cones lijiye aur unhein nok se nok mila dijiye, ek seedha aur ek ulta, aur zehan mein dono ko donon taraf be-hadd lamba kar dijiye. Yahi double cone hai. A dono ki milti hui nok (vertex) hai, RS beech wali seedhi line (axis) hai, aur A se surface ke saath saath jaane wali har tirchhi seedhi line generator hai. Upar wala aur neeche wala cone do nappes hain.
Ab is double cone ko ek chapti sheet (plane) se kaatiye. Kaat ka kinara ek curve hoga. Kaun sa curve banega, yeh sirf is baat par depend karta hai ke plane axis aur generator ke muqable mein kitni tirchhi (tilted) hai. Neeche Figure 6.1 mein har kaat ko side se dikhaya gaya hai: side se plane ek seedhi line nazar aati hai, aur curve woh mota hara hissa hai jahan plane cone ke andar hai.

blocks.alt: Four side views of a double cone with vertex A and axis RS. (a) a horizontal plane cuts one nappe: circle. (b) a slightly tilted plane cuts one nappe: ellipse. (c) a plane parallel to a generator cuts one nappe: parabola. (d) a plane parallel to the axis cuts both nappes: hyperbola.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.1(a)-(d): plane sections of a double cone, shown in side view (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: Plane ke angle aur position ke hisaab se aap ko circle, ellipse, parabola ya hyperbola milta hai. Kitab chaaron cases yun batati hai:

items: Agar kaatne wali plane axis par perpendicular ho to section (kaat) circle hota hai, Figure 6.1(a) dekhiye.
Agar plane thori si tirchhi (inclined) ho aur sirf ek nappe ko kaate to curve ellipse hota hai, Figure 6.1(b) dekhiye.
Agar plane kisi generator ke parallel ho aur sirf ek nappe ko kaate to curve parabola hota hai, Figure 6.1(c) dekhiye.
Agar plane axis ke parallel ho aur dono nappes ko kaate to curve hyperbola hota hai, Figure 6.1(d) dekhiye.

blocks.text: Hum apni study circle se shuru karenge. Baaqi conic sections agle sections mein aayenge.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein chhapa hai "We will being our study with the circle ... in subsequent section". Sahi angrezi yeh hai: "We will begin our study with the circle. Other conic sections will be discussed in subsequent sections."

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Chaaron cases yaad rakhne ka aasan tareeqa: plane ke jhukaav (tilt) ko generator ke jhukaav se compare kijiye.
1. Plane axis par bilkul perpendicular (koi jhukaav nahin): circle.
2. Plane jhuki hui, magar generator se kam dhalwan (steep): woh ek nappe ko poora aar paar kaat deti hai aur curve band ho jata hai: ellipse.
3. Plane bilkul generator jitni dhalwan (us ke parallel): curve kabhi band nahin hota, nappe ke saath saath door tak chalta jata hai: parabola.
4. Plane generator se bhi zyada dhalwan (masalan axis ke parallel): woh dono nappes ko kaat'ti hai: hyperbola, jis ki do alag shaakhein (branches) hoti hain.
Aage chal kar dekhenge ke chaaron curves ki equations \(x\) aur \(y\) mein second degree (yani square wali) hoti hain. Is unit mein: circle (6.1, 6.2), parabola (6.3), ellipse (6.4) aur hyperbola (6.5).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Degenerate conics ko thora aur khol kar dekhte hain, kyun ke exam mein in ka naam aksar poocha jata hai. Teenon shaklein tab banti hain jab plane bilkul vertex A se guzarti hai:
1. Plane A se guzre magar cone ki surface ko sirf A par chhooe (jaise axis par perpendicular plane jo theek nok par ho): kaat mein sirf ek point bachta hai. Yeh 'sikra hua circle ya ellipse' hai.
2. Plane A se guzre aur kisi generator ke saath saath lage (generator ke parallel aur us ko apne andar liye hue): kaat ek seedhi line hai. Yeh 'bigra hua parabola' hai.
3. Plane A se guzre aur dono nappes ko kaate (axis ke qareeb, zyada dhalwan): kaat do aapas mein katti hui seedhi lines hain. Yeh 'bigra hua hyperbola' hai.
Yani har asal conic ka ek degenerate roop hai jo plane ko vertex tak khiskaane se milta hai. Is liye kitab inhein 'special cases' kehti hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar plane bilkul vertex A se guzre aur axis par perpendicular ho to kaat mein kya bachega? (Jawab: sirf ek point, yani A. Yeh degenerate conic hai: circle jis ka radius zero ho gaya.)
Circle

Kitab ki definition: circle ek plane mein un tamaam points ka set hai jo ek diye hue fixed point se ek fixed faasle par hon. Fixed point ko centre kehte hain, aur fixed faasle ko circle ka radius kehte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh definition bilkul compass ka kaam hai: compass ki sui ek jagah tiki rehti hai (centre) aur pencil us se hamesha ek hi faasle par rehti hai (radius). Pencil jis jis point ko chhooti hai woh circle par hai, aur koi doosra point circle par nahin.
Is jumle ko equation mein badalne ke liye humein Class XI ka sirf ek auzaar chahiye: distance formula. Do points \((x_{1}, y_{1})\) aur \((x_{2}, y_{2})\) ke darmiyan faasla yeh hai:
\[d = \sqrt{(x_{2} - x_{1})^{2} + (y_{2} - y_{1})^{2}}\]
Yeh asal mein Pythagoras theorem hi hai: x ka farq ek side, y ka farq doosri side, aur faasla hypotenuse.
Theorem 1: Jis circle ka centre point \((h, k)\) aur radius \(r\) ho, us ki equation \((x - h)^{2} + (y - k)^{2} = r^{2}\) hai.

blocks.alt: Axes OX and OY. A circle with centre C(h, k); a radius r joins C to a point P(x, y) on the circle.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.2: circle with centre C(h, k) and radius r (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text:
Proof: Sab se pehle dekhte hain ke humare paas kya hai. Maan lijiye \(C(h, k)\) circle ka centre hai aur \(r\) us ka radius. \(P(x, y)\) circle par koi bhi point hai (koi khaas point nahin, balke 'har' point ki numaindagi). Definition ke mutabiq faasla \(|\overline{CP}|\) barabar hai \(r\) ke. Ab \(P(x, y)\) aur \(C(h, k)\) ke darmiyan distance formula lagate hain:
\[\sqrt{(x - h)^{2} + (y - k)^{2}} = r\]
Square root se jaan chhudane ke liye dono sides ka square lete hain:
\[(x - h)^{2} + (y - k)^{2} = r^{2} \quad \text{...(1)}\]
Yahi circle ki required equation hai. Ghor kijiye: humne "har point P" ke liye yeh baat saabit ki, is liye yeh equation poore circle ko describe karti hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Dono sides ka square lena yahan bilkul mehfooz (safe) kyun hai? Kyun ke dono sides faasle (lengths) hain, yani kabhi negative nahin. Do non-negative numbers barabar hon to un ke squares bhi barabar, aur squares barabar hon to numbers bhi barabar. Is liye (1) ko satisfy karne wala har point centre se \(r\) faasle par hai, aur ulta bhi sach hai.
Equation parhne ka tareeqa: \(x\) aur \(y\) mein se jo numbers minus ho rahe hain woh centre ke coordinates hain, aur right side radius ka square hai. Misal: \((x - 3)^{2} + (y + 4)^{2} = 25\) ko \((x - 3)^{2} + (y - (-4))^{2} = 5^{2}\) likh sakte hain, is liye centre \((3, -4)\) aur radius 5. Bracket mein plus ho to centre ka coordinate minus hota hai; yeh sign ulat jaane wali baat zehan mein bitha lijiye.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text:
(i) Equation (1) ko circle ki equation ki standard form kehte hain.
(ii) Agar \(r = 0\) ho to equation (1) ban jati hai \((x - h)^{2} + (y - k)^{2} = 0\). Yeh centre \((h, k)\) wala point circle hai.
(iii) Agar \((h, k) = (0, 0)\) ho to equation (1) ban jati hai \(x^{2} + y^{2} = r^{2}\). Yeh us circle ki equation hai jis ka centre origin par hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Point circle ko aise samjhiye: radius ko chhota karte jayein to circle sikurta jata hai, aur radius zero ho jaye to sirf centre bachta hai. \((x - h)^{2} + (y - k)^{2} = 0\) tabhi sach hai jab dono squares zero hon (kyun ke squares kabhi negative nahin hote, un ka jama zero tabhi hoga jab dono zero hon), yani sirf ek point \((h, k)\).
Aur agar right side negative ho, jaise \((x - 1)^{2} + y^{2} = -4\), to koi real point is ko satisfy nahin karta, kyun ke squares ka jama kabhi negative nahin ho sakta. Yeh case hum 6.1.2 mein dobara dekhenge.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin.) Centre \((4, -3)\) aur radius 6 wale circle ki equation likhiye.
\(h = 4\), \(k = -3\), \(r = 6\). Standard form mein rakhein:
\[(x - 4)^{2} + (y + 3)^{2} = 36\]
Dhyan dein: \(y - (-3) = y + 3\), aur \(6^{2} = 36\).
Ulta sawal: \(x^{2} + (y - 2)^{2} = 7\) ka centre aur radius? \(x^{2} = (x - 0)^{2}\), is liye centre \((0, 2)\) aur radius \(\sqrt{7}\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Ab ek aham sawal: kya har circle ki equation is standard form mein likhi ja sakti hai? Haan. Kisi bhi circle ka ek centre aur ek radius hota hai, aur upar wala proof kisi bhi \(h, k, r\) ke liye chalta hai. Is liye standard form har circle ke liye kaam karti hai.
Standard form ka sab se bara faida yeh hai ke is mein centre aur radius seedhe nazar aate hain. Jab sawal mein centre aur radius diye hon (ya aasaani se mil sakte hon), to hamesha isi form se shuru kijiye. Agle sabaq (6.1.2) mein hum is ko khol kar general form banayenge, jis mein centre aur radius chhup jate hain aur unhein nikaalne ke liye thori mehnat karni parti hai.
Ek aur baat: kisi point ko circle par check karna ho to us ke coordinates equation mein rakhiye. Agar left side theek \(r^{2}\) ke barabar aaye to point circle par hai; kam aaye to andar, zyada aaye to bahar. (Yeh idea 6.2.4 mein poori tarah aayega.)

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Circle \((x + 1)^{2} + (y + 1)^{2} = 2\) kya origin se guzarta hai? (Origin rakh kar dekhiye: \(1 + 1 = 2\). Haan, guzarta hai. Wajah bhi samajh lijiye: centre \((-1, -1)\) se origin ka faasla \(\sqrt{1 + 1} = \sqrt{2}\) hai, jo bilkul radius ke barabar hai.)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Double cone ko plane se kaatne par circle, ellipse, parabola ya hyperbola milta hai; plane vertex se guzre to degenerate conic (point, line ya do lines).
2. Circle: woh tamaam points jo ek fixed point (centre) se fixed faasle \(r\) (radius) par hon.
3. Standard form: \((x - h)^{2} + (y - k)^{2} = r^{2}\); centre \((h, k)\), radius \(r\).
4. Centre origin par ho to \(x^{2} + y^{2} = r^{2}\).
5. \(r = 0\) ho to point circle (sirf centre).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Centre ke sign ulte parhna: \((x + 2)^{2} + (y - 1)^{2} = 25\) ka centre \((-2, 1)\) hai, \((2, -1)\) nahin.
2. Right side ko hi radius samajh lena: \((x - 3)^{2} + y^{2} = 16\) ka radius \(\sqrt{16} = 4\) hai, 16 nahin.
3. Equation likhte waqt radius ka square bhool jana: radius 5 ho to right side 25 aayega, 5 nahin.
